_comment: Rules for the workspace pre-publish audit, run against whatever ref is
about to be pushed:
python ../.claude/skills/pre-publish-audit/audit_publish.py \
--ref main --rules .publish-audit.json
`deny` holds strings the built-in patterns cannot know about, because they
look like ordinary words to a generic scanner: the provider's brand host,
its CDN host label, the M3U account name suffixes, this installation's LAN
prefix, and this machine's drive mappings. Every pattern here is written
with a character class so that this rules file does not itself become the
leak it is meant to prevent.
`allow` holds expected placeholders and fixtures. Each needs a reason.
Loosening a pattern to silence a finding is how the next real one gets
through: add an allow entry with a reason instead.
THIS REPOSITORY IS PUBLIC AND IS PUSHED DIRECTLY, with no orphan branch
between the development history and GitHub. Measured 2026-08-05: public,
50 stars, 4 forks. There is therefore no second chance and no staging
step. Everything reachable from a pushed ref is world-readable the moment
the push completes, and with forks in existence a history rewrite cannot
take it back.
ALREADY PUBLISHED, recorded here so nobody rediscovers it as if it were
new: 33 blob references under docs/superpowers/ are reachable from
origin/main. Commit c40014c removed those design documents from the tree
and gitignored them, but removing a file from HEAD does not remove it from
history. An old settings-field placeholder carrying the private address
An old settings-field placeholder carrying a private address is likewise
reachable, from commits facb5f8 and 173efc2. The value itself is not
repeated here: this file is published, and the allow entry below's
pattern is the authority on it.
Neither is a credential. The decision, taken by the operator on
2026-08-05, is to accept both rather than rewrite history: a rewrite does
not reach the 4 forks or any cached view, and it would create a false
impression that the content had been withdrawn.

deny.why: the provider's real brand host, written as a pattern so this file does not contain it

the provider's real CDN host label, in any form. Swapping only the top-level domain is not a redaction: it still names the provider. Use edge-NN.example in fixtures instead, so this rule can stay absolute
the real M3U account name suffixes, one per provider login. They look like ordinary short words to a generic scanner
this installation's LAN prefix, which names the operator's internal network. The built-in private-address rule also catches it, but only at medium severity; naming it here makes it high
the live Dispatcharr host on this installation's LAN, as distinct from a documentation example
this machine's Windows drive mapping of the container volumes
an internal backup location on the live box, not a path any user of this plugin has
the operator's notes backup location, which names a private directory on a separate drive

allow.reason: The line in tests/test_publish_hygiene.py that lists the notes filenames the test refuses to let become tracked. A guard has to name what it guards against, and the built-in notes-reference rule is case-insensitive so it matches those names. Anchored to this one line so the same strings are still reported everywhere else in the repository

Textual references to the notes FILENAME, in .gitignore (the ignore rule itself), DEVELOPMENT.md, README.md, bump_version.py, pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml and tests/test_version_sync.py. No notes file is tracked and none of these lines carry notes CONTENT. This allowance also silences the scanner's file-NAME check for that string, so the real risk is covered precisely by tests/test_publish_hygiene.py, which fails if any file named CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE-HISTORY.md ever becomes tracked. Do not remove that test while this entry exists

Textual references to the design-document directory NAME, in .gitignore (the ignore rules) and one docstring in tests/test_black_screen.py citing the spec a feature came from. Nothing under docs/superpowers/ is tracked. As with the CLAUDE.md entry above, the file-NAME check is covered instead by tests/test_publish_hygiene.py, which fails if any tracked path contains that directory

A deliberate test fixture in iptv_checker/plugin.py and tests/test_scheduler_host_eligibility.py. The scheduler excludes the daphne ASGI process from the cross-process election by matching a command-line token BASENAME rather than a raw substring, so that a plugin installed under a path like /home/daphne/ is not wrongly excluded, which would leave the deployment with no scheduler host at all. It is a path shape under test, not anyone's home directory

Documentation placeholders for a Dispatcharr URL in plugin settings help text and README examples. Neither is this installation's address: the live host is covered by its own deny entry above. The second alternative in this pattern is additionally present in already-published history, recorded in the comment block at the top of this file

_private_remotes_comment: Remotes that legitimately receive the development history, including the
notes and any design documents. The pre-push hook skips its content audit
for these and only for these.
THIS REPOSITORY HAS NO SUCH REMOTE. origin is a PUBLIC publication target,
so it must always be audited. An unrecognised remote is audited, which
means the default stays deny and this empty list is the correct state, not
an oversight. Do not add origin here to silence a finding.
